result_text:
Template literals are now masked the same way as `"..."` and `'...'` literals when units are compared for duplication. The existing tests in `CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractorTest`, `UnitsExtractorTest` and `DuplicationEngineTest` pass. I didn't add a test, and I didn't run the two-function example (`` `Hello alpha ${name}` `` vs `` `Hello beta ${name}` ``) end to end.

The change is one line in `extraCleanContent` in `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/units/CStyleHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`:

```java
cleanedContent = cleanedContent.replaceAll("`.*?`", "``");
```

It sits right after the single-quote rule and before the slash rule. A template literal, including its `${...}` part, collapses to ``` `` ```, so only differences outside the literals keep two units apart.

Only template literals that open and close on the same line are masked. A literal spanning several lines is left alone. Masking it would shift the line mapping the extractor relies on.
